nodes.label: No validated real-video accuracy
nodes.rationale: The 94% accuracy and 0.982 AUC are from a random holdout of the same synthetic signal generator; they do not measure accuracy on genuine or deepfake videos and no cross-dataset test has been run.

nodes.label: rPPG is not a deepfake detector on its own
nodes.rationale: A physiologically plausible pulse only shows the video is not obviously a class of deepfake that fails to preserve blood-flow cues; some synthesis methods preserve physiological signal and REAL videos can score poorly due to lighting, compression or motion.

nodes.label: Signal-quality gating is a heuristic
nodes.rationale: The SNR-to-quality mapping and the confidence-discounting curve are heuristics, not fitted to labelled ground truth (e.g. Platt scaling), so they must be calibrated against a verified video benchmark before being read as probabilities.

nodes.label: MediaPipe face detection dependency and fail-closed behaviour
nodes.rationale: MediaPipe Face Landmarker needs a downloaded .task model file; videos with no detectable face fail closed with 'no usable signal' rather than a wrong prediction, but coverage on low-quality footage is inherently limited.

nodes.label: Motion, lighting and compression sensitivity
nodes.rationale: Green/CHROM/POS are all sensitive to head motion, illumination change and heavy compression regardless of whether the video is real or fake, which is why warnings explicitly separate 'reasons this measurement might be unreliable' from evidence for/against authenticity.

nodes.label: Harmonic ratio unreliable without a real dominant peak
nodes.rationale: 'Energy near 2x/3x the peak' is only meaningful when the peak is a real cardiac frequency; on pure noise the ratio can score higher than on a real signal. Neutralised by signal-quality gating rather than fixed at the source.

nodes.label: Codebase generation environment constraints
nodes.rationale: The scientific core was written and tested end-to-end with NumPy/SciPy/OpenCV/MediaPipe/scikit-learn, while the Node/Express API and React frontend could not be npm-installed or run in the generation environment (no network), so the first local run is where integration bugs are most likely to surface.
